thread:
rachel: Heads up  noticed a flurry of mtls handshake rejects in staging and prod eu this morning after the keystore RBAC rollout. Proxy sidecars returning 502s and keystore logs show early RBAC denies. Anyone oncall?

juan: Yep seeing it too on the dashboards. Which principal is failing?

rachel: svc-proxy in eu-west-3 primarily. Sample keystore log: 
```
2026-04-14T07:12:02Z keystore-3 INFO rbac: principal=svc-proxy.eu-west-3 check=decrypt result=DENY reason=subject-missing-in-rolebinding
```

natasha: That 'subject-missing' is worrying. We recently changed the renderer used by our infra pipeline (render-keystore-bindings v2) to avoid hardcoding namespaces. Looks like in some clusters it emitted subjects like 'system:serviceaccount:infra:svc-proxy' and in others just 'svc-proxy' due to a template var being empty.

ops-oncall: I can patch the RoleBinding in prod-eu quickly. Before we mutate, collect artifacts: kube-audit event for the RoleBinding apply, keystore pod logs (last 20m), proxy sidecar logs (peer_cert_sha256, SNI), and the RoleBinding yaml. Also snapshot the rendered manifest that pipeline applied.

juan: grabbing proxy logs now. Quick grep: 
```
kubectl -n services logs proxy-abc --since=15m | grep peer_cert_sha256 | head -n 3
```

keystore-bot: Forensics helper created trace id fk-20260414-0713. Use to correlate keystore logs and audit sink.

natasha: devops: the render-keystore-bindings change used server-side apply and we discovered a nilvalue in the region mapping that caused namespace interpolation to drop. Pipeline job: https://ci.internal/pipelines/render-keystore-bindings/295. I’ll revert the template and re-render.

ops-oncall: Rolling a minimal fix to RoleBinding in eu to restore explicit subjects: 
```
kubectl --context=eu-prod -n infra apply -f /manifests/keystore/fix-rolebinding-eu.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore -n infra
```

rachel: note: KMS audit doesn't show decrypt attempts for those principals because keystore has an early-authorize path to avoid KMS QPS. We should emit an audit event to our logshipper even when early-deny occurs so we have evidence.

juan: Patch applied and keystore restarted. Watching metrics...

~7 minutes later~

rachel: Handshake failures down from 3.1% -> 0.2% in eu cluster. Looks recovered.

natasha: Postmortem items: 1) fix renderer to always emit full namespace-qualified subject string, add unit tests for region mappings; 2) add a pipeline preflight that `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:svc-proxy decrypt` or run an in-cluster canary decrypt job; 3) change keystore to emit an audit_stub to logshipper whenever it returns early DENY with fields: principal, reason, sni, peer_cert_sha256, trace_id.

ops-oncall: Also recommend changing the RBAC rollout process to include a dry-run validation that checks `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra -o jsonpath=..subjects[*]` and fail if expected subjects missing.

keystore-bot: Planned change: add `audit_stub_id` and `rbac_eval_trace` to keystore logs, and a config flag `keystore.emit_earlydeny_audit=true` default false for now.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-072 created: "EU mTLS rejects after keystore binding renderer change". Severity: P2. Please attach timeline and manifests to PR.

juan: I'll open the PR to revert the renderer default and add explicit namespace interpolation tests. natasha: assign to you for review.

rachel: Follow-up checklist for PR: include sample failed logs, kube-audit event, rendered manifest snapshot, and runbook update to include the new canary check.

natasha: will add integration test that simulates missing subject and asserts keystore early-deny emits audit_stub to logshipper. Also adding a CI gate to assert that all rolebinding subjects are namespace-qualified strings.

ops-oncall: Short-term alert tweak: if mtls_handshake_denied_rate{region=\"eu\"} > 0.5% for 3m -> page and runbook step 1 is to `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-* -o jsonpath='{.subjects}'`.

rachel: thanks all. Blameless postmortem planned for tomorrow. Let's keep this focused on preventing template regressions and improving telemetry.
